display.purpose: Kiosk hero moments and page identity blocks. Never used on form headers.

title.purpose: Card titles, section leaders, table headers.

body.purpose: Default paragraph and control label. Line length capped at 65-75ch for prose.

label.purpose: Uppercase structural section markers only. Never as ornamental eyebrows above every section.

amharic-body.purpose: Amharic Fidel gets its own body ramp: +1px size and +0.15 line-height over Latin because Fidel glyphs are visually taller and need vertical breathing room.

shadows.name: state-response
shadows.purpose: Card hover lift. Never present at rest.

shadows.name: floating-chrome
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, dropdowns, popovers that escape the document flow.

shadows.name: focus-ring-brass
shadows.purpose: Focus indicator on interactive elements. Ministry Brass at 40% opacity, offset 2px.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions. Snappy without bounce.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Reveal / expand transitions where a more dramatic ease-out reads intentional.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition duration for panels, tabs, and other UI state changes.

narrative.overview:
The system reads as an unmistakably state-run institution that has taken the trouble to welcome you. Every surface is warm enough for a citizen unfamiliar with digital wayfinding to feel invited, and formal enough that no one mistakes it for a startup product. Officialdom is a floor, not a ceiling: the Ministry's authority sits in the confidence of the type, the depth of Highland Petrol on the sidebar, the honest weight of Ministry Brass on primary actions — never in ornament, seals, or theatre.

The identity is carried by two colors, one script pair, and generous whitespace. Highland Petrol grounds the interface as a state-run touchpoint; Ministry Brass earns its place on the ~10% of surface that carries the decision. Nothing else needs to shout. Amharic Fidel is a first-class language throughout — its own line-height, its own comfortable size, never crammed into metrics tuned for Latin.

This system explicitly rejects the generic dark-gradient SaaS dashboard, the 2005-era government intranet, fake-corporate ministry aesthetics, any "Africa cliche" ornamentation, Web3 / crypto energy, startup cheerfulness, and the AI-slop defaults. If a page looks like it came from a generic AI generator, it has failed.
keyCharacteristics: Bilingual by construction — English and Amharic Fidel are equal-weight throughout.
Two-color identity — Highland Petrol carries the surface, Ministry Brass carries the decision.
Flat by default — depth is a state response, not a resting condition.
Kiosk-native — the public screen isn't a shrunken desktop; it's built for 2–3 metre viewing.
Craft signals care — spacing, typography, and motion demonstrate the ministry's respect for its citizens.

rules.name: The Two-Color Rule
rules.body: Highland Petrol carries surface identity, Ministry Brass carries the decision. Everything else is neutral. If a design needs a third color, the answer is either weight, size, or a rule change — never a new hue.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Ministry Brass appears on ≤ 10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. When a design shows brass on multiple cards, on borders, on chips, and on buttons in the same view, the surface has been diluted; strip it back to the single most important call-to-action.

rules.name: The Bilingual Parity Rule
rules.body: Amharic Fidel and Latin are equal-weight throughout. Fidel is never smaller, never lower-contrast, never in a fallback font stack. When both languages appear side by side, both get equal typographic weight; when only Amharic renders, the entire surface must read as native, not translated.

rules.name: The Kicker Restraint Rule
rules.body: The uppercase Label is reserved for structural section headers (sidebar section names, table column headers). Placing a small uppercase kicker above every content section is the current AI grammar tell — this system refuses it. Structure earns the label; ornament doesn't.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Every surface starts flat. If a component needs elevation, the reviewer's question is not "what shadow?" but "what state is this responding to?" Elevation is earned by interaction (hover, focus, active) or by legitimately escaping the document flow (dialog, popover) — never by design reflex.

rules.name: The No Nested Cards Rule
rules.body: A raised surface inside another raised surface is always wrong. If content needs grouping inside a card, use spacing, a thin hairline, or a Quiet Surface panel — never a second card.

dos: Do use Highland Petrol as the surface identity color (sidebar, primary text, headers) and Ministry Brass strictly for the decision (primary CTA, active nav item, published-status indicator).
Do treat Amharic Fidel as a first-class language: same visual weight, its own line-height and size ramps, native font stack via next/font.
Do cap body prose line length at 65-75ch — including on the kiosk, where wider blocks become harder to scan across the room.
Do ensure body text hits ≥4.5:1 contrast (WCAG AA); ≥7:1 (AAA) is the target across both admin and kiosk surfaces.
Do use text-wrap: balance on H1-H3 for even line lengths, and text-wrap: pretty on long prose to reduce orphans.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every animated element — every animation must have a defined stationary alternative.
Do verify contrast against the ambient light expected in the ministry lobby, not just the WCAG ratio in isolation.
donts: Don't use a purple gradient hero, an Inter body font, nested cards, or tiny gray body text on a tinted near-white background. That specific combination is the AI-slop default that PRODUCT.md forbids.
Don't style this like a generic dark-gradient SaaS dashboard (Vercel / Stripe / Linear / crypto-tool aesthetic).
Don't revert to the 2005-era government intranet template — no tiny 11px body text, no blue underlined links as a default, no tables inside tables.
Don't decorate with "Africa cliche" motifs — no acacia trees, no giraffes, no traditional patterns applied as ornamental texture.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient background). Decorative, never meaningful.
Don't use glassmorphism as a default. Blurs and glass surfaces are rare and purposeful, or they don't appear at all.
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent on cards, list items, or callouts.
Don't stack cards inside cards. If a card needs internal grouping, use spacing or a Quiet Surface panel — never a second card.
Don't put a small uppercase kicker above every content section (the ABOUT / PROCESS / PRICING pattern).
Don't use numbered section markers as scaffolding (01 / 02 / 03) unless the section genuinely IS a sequence.
Don't ship a Corporate government aesthetic (stock handshake photos, generic globe icons, everything-blue).
Don't pair Geist with a similar-but-not-identical geometric sans (Inter, Manrope, DM Sans). Pair on a contrast axis or use Geist in multiple weights.
Don't animate CSS layout properties unless truly needed. Transform and opacity only, with ease-out-quart / quint / expo easing.
Don't ship any surface that looks like a generic AI generator produced it.
